inflation.title: Inflation in Spain (INE)
inflation.subtitle: Headline CPI · {{rate}} · {{period}}
inflation.note: Last {{count}} months published by INE (series IPC251856).
inflation.empty: Not enough data points for the chart yet.
inflation.helpAria: What Spanish inflation is and how to read this chart
inflation.help:
What it measures: how much consumer prices have risen on average over the past 12 months.

How to read it: each point is that month's year-on-year change. A rising line means inflation is accelerating; a falling line means it is slowing (prices may still be going up).

Why it matters: it erodes cash purchasing power and informs the inflation assumption in your projections.

interestRate.title: 12-month Euribor (ECB)
interestRate.subtitle: Monthly average · {{rate}} · {{period}}
interestRate.note: Last {{count}} months published by the ECB (EURIBOR1YD series).
interestRate.empty: Not enough data points for the chart yet.
interestRate.helpAria: What 12-month Euribor is and how to read this chart
interestRate.help:
What it measures: the rate at which banks lend to each other for 12 months in the euro area.

How to read it: most variable mortgages in Spain reset on 12M Euribor + spread. If the line rises, your payment will likely rise at the next annual review.

Why it matters: it signals changes in one of your largest fixed costs if you have a variable-rate mortgage.

coreInflation.title: Underlying CPI (INE)
coreInflation.subtitle: Excl. food & energy · {{rate}} · {{period}}
coreInflation.note: Last {{count}} months published by INE (series IPC292510).
coreInflation.empty: Not enough data points for the chart yet.
coreInflation.helpAria: What underlying CPI is and how to read this chart
coreInflation.help:
What it measures: inflation excluding unprocessed food and energy, which tend to swing sharply month to month.

How to read it: usually smoother than headline CPI. If headline rises but core does not, much of the spike may be temporary (power, fuel…).

Why it matters: the ECB watches it closely; it reflects more persistent price pressures than headline CPI.

depositRate.title: ECB deposit rate
depositRate.subtitle: Deposit facility · {{rate}} · {{period}}
depositRate.note: Last {{count}} months (last daily value each month, DFR.LEV series).
depositRate.empty: Not enough data points for the chart yet.
depositRate.helpAria: What the ECB deposit rate is and how to read this chart
depositRate.help:
What it measures: the rate the ECB pays banks on money they leave on deposit at the Eurosystem.

How to read it: it only changes when the ECB decides (steps, not a smooth curve). Flat stretches mean the same rate for months.

Why it matters: it sets a floor for savings accounts and deposits; banks usually pay a bit more to attract customers.
